# Vendored PouchDB test files

Spec 03 task 1 decision: vendor real spec files from `apache/pouchdb`'s
`tests/integration/` rather than write a bespoke suite. PouchDB doesn't publish an
installable conformance package, and third-party adapters that get its suite "for
free" (e.g. `pouchdb-adapter-fs`) all do so by building on
`pouchdb-adapter-leveldb-core` — a key/value seam. This adapter deliberately isn't
that (ADR-0001: document-level seam, no leveldown interface), so there's no
off-the-shelf path; vendoring real upstream files is the most faithful alternative to
spec 03's "PouchDB's adapter conformance suite passes in full."

Every vendored file's `adapters` array must be trimmed to `['local']` — there is no
CouchDB `http` target in this project.

| File | Vendored from | Modifications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test.aa.setup.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.aa.setup.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `require('../../packages/node_modules/pouchdb/package.json')` → `require('pouchdb-core/package.json')` — the upstream path only resolves inside the pouchdb monorepo; we depend on `pouchdb-core` directly, not the `pouchdb` meta-package. |
| `test.local_docs.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.local_docs.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed from `['http', 'local']` to `['local']` only, per the rule above. No other changes — passes as-is against `_getLocal`/`_putLocal`/`_removeLocal` (spec 03 task 2), including the `"0-N"`/`"0-0"` rev format and conflict-detection semantics this task added to the `putLocal`/`removeLocal` native contract specifically to make this file pass unmodified. |
| `test.bulk_docs.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.bulk_docs.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. `test/testUtils.js` grew `errors` (re-exports `pouchdb-errors`, the real package this adapter already depends on), `rev` (from `pouchdb-utils`, matching upstream's own `pouchUtils.rev` — see below), and stub `isCouchDB`/`isSafari`/`isCouchMaster` (always false/`cb(false)` — this project never runs against a real CouchDB or in a browser, but the vendored file still calls these directly). Vendoring this file surfaced a real native-contract gap: two concurrent `_bulkDocs` calls to the same brand-new doc id both succeeded silently (no conflict) because `bulkWrite` unconditionally overwrote whatever was stored, with nothing checking that the tree JS merged against was still current (`handles simultaneous writes`). Fixed across all three repos by adding `WriteOp.expectedPrevWinningRev` (a compare-and-swap token, not a tree-semantics decision — ADR-0001 still holds) that `bulkWrite` checks per op, rejecting (not batch-failing) any op whose assumption has gone stale; see `specs/02-docstack-store.md`. Originally 12 cases skipped (9 needing `_allDocs`/`_changes` — spec 03 task 4); task 4 landed `_allDocs`/`_changes` for real, so those 9 were un-skipped and now pass. The remaining 2 (`4372 revs_limit ... deletes old revisions of the doc`, plain and `auto_compaction: true` variants) needed spec 03 task 7's real compaction and are now un-skipped too — see the task 7 write-up in `test.basics.js`'s row for the shared `revs_limit`/`auto_compaction` fix. 0 remain skipped. |
| `test.basics.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.basics.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. Vendoring this file surfaced two real gaps, both fixed across all repos: `info().doc_count` counted every doc regardless of deletion (`db.info should give correct doc_count`) instead of excluding docs whose winning revision is deleted, per CouchDB's own semantics — fixed in `InMemoryDocumentStore`, `RocksDbDocumentStore`, and the fake carrier; and `db.id()` had no adapter method at all (`this._id` was simply never assigned, not even stubbed, causing `db.id()` to hang rather than fail) — added `_id`, backed by a reserved `_local/instanceId` local doc reusing the existing `putLocal`/`getLocal` primitives, same pattern the reference `pouchdb-adapter-leveldb-core` uses (a persisted-UUID metadata key), just riding the local-doc contract instead of a bespoke one. Originally 21 cases skipped; task 4 landing `_allDocs`/`_changes` un-skipped 7 of them (including two "Fail to fetch a doc..." variants), leaving one of those two still skipped for a *different*, newly-exposed reason (see below). Task 7 (`_doCompaction`, `_destroy`, `_close`) un-skipped the 13 needing `_destroy`/`_close` directly. It also surfaced a real gap along the way, found via the `test.bulk_docs.js` `4372 ...` cases (see that row): `merge()`'s `revs_limit` stemming (already wired into `_bulkDocs` since task 3) only ever pruned the *tree* - the cut revisions' bodies stayed in native storage forever, still fetchable by explicit rev, since `_get` reads directly by `(id, rev)` regardless of tree membership. Fixed by threading `merge()`'s own `stemmedRevs` return value through to a `compact()` crossing right after a successful write (no native contract change - reuses the existing `compact(db, id, revs, tree)` capability `_doCompaction` also uses). Tracing the `auto_compaction: true` variant of that same test surfaced a second, related gap: `auto_compaction` isn't wired to anything in `pouchdb-core@9` itself (confirmed by reading its source - real disk-based adapters implement it themselves), and it means something *stronger* than `revs_limit`-bounded stemming - compact to leaves-only on every write. Fixed by additionally running `pouchdb-merge`'s `compactTree()` (which marks every non-leaf `'available'` node missing, a superset-safe operation since it skips anything `merge()` already stemmed) when `opts.auto_compaction` is set. 3 remain skipped: 2 need the `pouchdb-replication` plugin (`db.replicate`), which this harness never loads — out of scope for a local-only adapter, not a gap; 1 (`putting is override-able`) can't pass under any adapter as written — it calls `db.put(doc)` with no trailing callback and then asserts a monkey-patched `put` saw one, a legacy `initPull`/`cleanupPut` replication-hook pattern `pouchdb-core@9` doesn't wire up this way anymore. |
| `test.get.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.get.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. `test/testUtils.js` grew `putAfter`/`putBranch`/`putTree`/`writeDocs`, ported verbatim from upstream's `utils.js` (needed to build synthetic rev trees for conflict/branch tests) — this is what pulled `pouchdb-utils` from a test-only devDependency into a real production `dependencies` entry, since `_id` (added while triaging `test.basics.js`, see above) also needs `pouchdb-utils`'s `uuid()`. 7 cases skipped, all the `5857 - ... latest=true` family — `_get`'s `latest` option (resolve to a branch's current leaf instead of the literal requested rev) was already explicitly deferred in `src/index.ts`'s `_get` doc comment back in spec 03 task 2 ("`revs`/`open_revs`/`conflicts` options need real multi-revision trees to mean anything and are follow-up work"); vendoring this file just gave that deferral concrete failing test cases, not a new discovery. |
| `test.all_docs.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.all_docs.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. Vendoring this file surfaced a real native-contract gap, fixed across all repos: `total_rows` in `_all_docs` was computed from the *filtered* result set (after `startkey`/`endkey`/`keys` restriction), so it changed with every query — CouchDB's own `_all_docs` semantics are that `total_rows` is always the whole database's non-deleted doc count, completely independent of the query (`rows`/`offset` are the only things a query affects). Fixed in `InMemoryDocumentStore`, `RocksDbDocumentStore`, and the fake carrier; pinned with a new conformance test (`allDocs_totalRows_isTheWholeDatabasesNonDeletedCount_regardlessOfQuery`). Also fixed adapter-side: a deleted doc row with `include_docs: true` returned a stub tombstone body instead of `doc: null`, per CouchDB's own convention. Task 7 un-skipped `test after db close` (needed `_close`). 3 remain skipped: 2 (`Testing all docs`, `#3082 test wrong num results returned`) aren't adapter-specific — both use `.should.be.at.least(...)`/`.at.most(...)`/`.above(...)` on string ids, and chai 4.5.0's implementation of those assertions only ever accepts numbers or dates ("expected '0' to be a number or a date"), failing identically under any adapter with this pinned chai version; 1 (`Testing conflicts`) needs `_changes`'s `conflicts`/`style: 'all_docs'` options, already deferred (see `test.changes.js` below). |
| `test.changes.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.changes.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. Vendoring this file surfaced three real bugs in `_changes`, all fixed: (1) the non-live path only fetched doc bodies when `include_docs` was requested, but a `filter` function (plain, or a ddoc/view/selector filter — `pouchdb-changes-filter` normalizes all of those to a function before `_changes` ever sees them) needs the body to evaluate against regardless of whether the caller wants it in the output, so every filtered-changes call was silently dropping every doc; (2) `limit` was passed straight to native, which applies it to the *pre-filter* candidate set — with a JS-side filter present this silently truncated before the filter ever ran, losing matches past the cut; fixed to fetch unlimited and count the limit against post-filter matches instead, same as the reference adapter's per-row stream approach. Vendoring also surfaced two bugs in the *test-only* fake carrier (not native, not the adapter): `subscribeChanges` never replayed already-committed writes from `since`, contradicting `DocumentStore.subscribeChanges`'s own documented contract (spec 02) that the real Kotlin engines already implement and test; and once replay was added, it fired synchronously *during* `subscribeChanges()` itself, which runs synchronously inside `db.changes(...)` — before PouchDB core's chained `.on('change', ...)` had even been attached, so every replayed event fired into a void. Fixed by snapshotting synchronously (race-free) but deferring the actual `listener()` calls to a microtask. Task 7 un-skipped the 2 needing `_destroy`/`_close`. 9 remain skipped: 2 need `_changes`'s `style: 'all_docs'` option (needs a real per-doc rev tree, deferred — see `test.all_docs.js` above); 1 needs the `pouchdb-replication` plugin, not loaded in this harness; 2 aren't adapter-specific — `assert.isRejected(promise, 'completes with an exception')` treats its second argument as a message-content matcher (confirmed against chai-as-promised's own `rejectedWith()` overloads), and the actual rejection (a correct 404 `not_found` `MISSING_DOC` for the absent design doc) never carries that literal text under any local adapter; 1 (`Changes accepts "_design" as filter property`) expects a CouchDB server-side built-in filter (`_design`) that `pouchdb-changes-filter` doesn't implement client-side (unlike `_view`, which it does special-case) — fails identically under any local adapter. |
| `test.revs_diff.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.revs_diff.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. No modifications otherwise, no skips — all 8 cases pass unmodified, including the conflicting-revisions and deleted-but-superseded-revision cases: native's `revs` column family already keeps every revision body ever written (not just the winning one), so `revsDiff` needs no tree-walking to answer them correctly. Vendoring this file didn't surface a native gap; it surfaced a documentation bug in `03-docstack-adapter.md` (see below) — `revsDiff`/`bulkGet` aren't `_`-prefixed hooks in `pouchdb-core@9`, unlike everything else this adapter overrides. |
| `test.bulk_get.js` | `apache/pouchdb`, `master`, `tests/integration/test.bulk_get.js` (fetched 2026-08-09) | `adapters` trimmed to `['local']`. 6 of 10 cases pass unmodified (rev-specified fetch, no-rev fetch, `_revisions` present/absent/with-implicit-rev, `#5886` reserved id `'constructor'` — grouping bulkGet's native results by id with a `Map`, not a plain object, was the one thing that needed care there, since a plain-object lookup table would resolve `'constructor'` to `Object.prototype.constructor` before any assignment). 4 skipped: 1 (`latest=true`) needs the same real-rev-tree branch resolution already deferred for `_get`'s `latest` option since task 2; 3 (`attachments are not included by default`, `attachments are included when specified` ×2) need spec 03 task 6 (native has no digest/blob storage yet). |

Files land here as the adapter methods they exercise are implemented (spec 03 tasks
2+), not all at once — task 1 only proves the harness runs a real upstream file at
all.
